title: Chicken Thighs With Apple, Fennel and Onion on a Sheet Pan
description: By Colu Henry: Chicken thighs are roasted with classic fall ingredients for a quick, flavorful sheet-pan supper. The toasted fennel seeds subtly amplify the anise flavor of the roasted fennel and play nicely with the apples and onions. Look for an apple on the tart side as it will naturally sweeten as it cooks in the oven. If you want to use bone-in chicken breasts you can, just make sure to cut the cooking time by a few minutes so they don’t dry out. Serve with a bright, bitter green salad flecked with blue cheese and toasted walnuts.
ingredients: 2½ to 3 pounds (4 to 6) bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, patted dry
1 medium yellow onion, thinly sliced (about 1½ cups)
1 medium fennel bulb, tough outer leaves removed, cored and thinly sliced (about 1 cup)
1 or 2 tart apples, cored and cut into 8 wedges
4 medium red potatoes or a baked potato sliced into 4 rounds
directions: In a small skillet, toast the fennel seeds over medium-low heat, stirring frequently until fragrant, about 2 to 3 minutes. Pound into a coarse powder with a mortar and pestle or, alternatively, roughly chop.
In a large bowl, toss together the chicken with 1 tablespoon olive oil and the fennel seeds and season well with salt and pepper.
Place the onion, fennel, and potato slices on the sheet pan. Toss with the remaining olive oil and season well with salt. Spread in an even layer.
Add the chicken skin side up on top of the vegetables and tuck the rosemary under the chicken. Roast for around 20 minutes

Add the apple wedges and continue to cook another 10 minutes or so, until the chicken is cooked through and the onions, fennel, potatoes, and apples are softened and have begun to caramelize at the edge of the pan.
If needed to get everything done and browned, turn the oven to broil and sear for 1 to 2 minutes until the skin of the chicken is crispy and golden. Season with flaky salt.
